newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Nedlloyd, P&O in container link.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nedlloyd, P&O in container link.

text.p: Dutch group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV and Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc said on Monday they planned a merger in container shipping that would create one of the world's biggest container fleets.

Nedlloyd and P&O will each take a 50 percent stake in a new company joining their container shipping interests, to be called P&O Nedlloyd Container Line. Nedlloyd will pay P&O $175 million to equalise the shareholdings.
"With a combined turnover of nearly $4 billion and a net asset value of some $1.5 billion, the new company will be one of the largest in world container shipping," a joint statement said.
P&O Nedlloyd, to be jointly chaired by Lord Sterling of P&O and Leo Berndsen of Nedlloyd, will begin operations by the year-end, following due diligence and regulatory procedures.
"The new company will have an excellent management team and a strong balance sheet. P&O Nedlloyd will be a world force in container shipping," Sterling said.

The new venture will have the world's biggest container ship fleet in terms of standing slots and an annual throughput of close to 2.5 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU). The TEU is the standard measure of volume in container shipping.
Headquartered in London but with its fleet managed from Rotterdam, it will operate 112 owned and chartered container ships and 540,000 TEU of owned and leased container boxes.
The companies said savings of over $200 million a year had already been identified from a total $3.9 billion cost base.
The savings will be achieved by losing up to 1,400 jobs from an existing combined workforce of around 9,400, greater network efficiency and reduced inland and terminal costs.
Nedlloyd will take a 200 million guilder extraordinary charge this year to cover the effects of the merger.

Finance director Haddo Meijer said the charge would result from a write-down in the value of ships which will be transferred to the newly formed venture, partially offsetting first-half extraordinary gains of 273 million guilders.
First-half net profit, aided by the one-off gain, came in at 276 million guilders versus 96 million in the 1995 first half.
Meijer said there was no change to Nedlloyd's forecast that it would not make a loss on ordinary operations this year.
In early Amsterdam trading, Nedlloyd shares gained 3.30 guilders, or over eight percent, to 42.80 guilders apiece. In London, P&O stock added six pence to 536 pence.
